chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Musicians as gentlemen
summary: McRae recalls musicians as dignified, well-dressed men, such as Coleman Hawkins strolling on 7th Avenue.

Very clean gentleman. Most of the musicians that you are reading about or talking about, these fellows were just like -- (inaudible) just like doctors. They carried theirself as gentleman -- you know, musicians back there. Thought very highly of themselves. If we went out in the afternoons Hampton, they would dress, like, you know.

First time I saw Coleman Hawkins walking down 7th Avenue, he had on this black coat -- dark gray coat with striped pants and his walking cane. Guy say (inaudible), "That's Coleman Hawkins." I say (inaudible), "No." (Inaudible), "Coleman, hi." He'd say, "Hi," you know. Very classy (inaudible). You know, (inaudible). And those are the days that musicians thought of -- everybody respect them, you know. and (inaudible) everybody looked up to the musicians in that (inaudible) day, you know -- you know, back in those days, you know.
